subtitle: One more mission against the Bydo

body: R-Type Final is Irem's PlayStation 2 horizontally scrolling shooter, first released in Japan on 17 July 2003. A pilot investigates the remains of an earlier battle before returning to the long war against the Bydo. The player advances through hostile stages in a small craft whose weapons and attached Force device determine how each danger can be approached. The title was intended as a farewell to the main series. Its stages, unlockable ships and accompanying fragments of writing turn that last mission into a survey of the strange universe R-Type had built.

Different craft and weapon arrangements change the options available against a familiar pattern. The Force can shield a vulnerable direction or extend an attack, making its position part of the player's response rather than an automatic accessory. Learning a stage involves recognising where a threat appears and deciding which part of the equipment should answer it. Unlocking additional ships gives that knowledge another use: a route already understood can be attempted with different strengths and limitations. The collection becomes a practical invitation to revisit the same hostile space.

Kazuma Kujo produced and designed the game, with Yuki Iwai composing the score. The campaign contains alternative routes and outcomes, giving its apparent conclusion more than one direction. North American and European editions followed in 2004. Despite the original intention behind its name, the series continued in other forms and eventually returned to scrolling action with R-Type Final 2 in 2021. The PlayStation 2 release retains the character of a retrospective farewell, gathering many machines and ideas around another attempt to understand and survive the Bydo.
